text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Striking magistrates were expected to resume work after successful discussions with the government over increased pay.
- A total of 2,500 villagers have been left homeless following torrential rains in the northern Lauapula Province.
- At least 18 people have died and 40 were admitted to hospital after a suspected plague caused by dead rats found in boreholes and wells for domestic use in southern Zambia.

- A memorandum of understanding between a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa and the Zambian government on the development of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines ZCCM.PA (ZCCM) Konkola Deep mine will be signed in February, mines minister Christon Tembo said.
- Zambia and Malawi rejected allegations by suspended Common Market of Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) Secretary-General Bingu Wa Mutharika that his suspension was politically motivated.
- A top World Bank official, John Todd, exposed the government's intention to introduce laws to control the press and non-governmental organisations.
- The independent Weekly Express has been ordered to pay a Catholic priest it libelled damages of 55 million kwacha ($50,000).
